## One Complete Example

`[clean-room]` - a full compile-and-run session, not copied from any manual.

```c
/* hello.c */
#include <stdio.h>

main()
{
    printf("Hello from OS-9\n");
}
```

Source files need CR-only line endings. A file written with an OS-9 editor
already has them; one brought over from a Unix host has LF endings and must be
converted before it reaches OS-9 (`common/using-os9exec-repl.md` covers the
host-side tools). Then compile and run:
```
cc hello.c
hello
```
`cc hello.c` produces an executable module named `hello` (no separate link
step for a single file). The compiler automatically links `LIB/cstart.r`
